title: hydraulic
intro:
This component is responsible for specifying the soils hydraulic properties.
    Used by horizon component hydraulic (see 47, page 231) , and Soil @ Hydraulic
(see 107.21, page 613) .

sections.name: B C inverse
sections.desc:
Campbell retention curve model with Burdine theory.
   This implementation is based on inverse modelling, you specify water at wilting
point (pF 4.2) and field capacity (pF 2.0), from which the retention curve (the b and
h b parameters) is derived. Based on this, the condutivity curve is fully specified
by a single point. See also [Campbell, 1974, Burdine, 1953]
sections.sig:
< B C inverse        (Theta sat Theta sat )
                       (K sat K sat )
                       (K at h K at h )
                       (Theta fc Theta fc )
                       (Theta wp Theta wp ) >

sections.name: MACRO
sections.desc:
van Genuchten retention curve model with Mualem theory. The near saturated
retention and hydraulic properties have been adjusted to take macropores into ac-
count. See also [Larsbo and Jarvis, 2003]
sections.sig:
< MACRO (alpha alpha )
              (Theta sat Theta sat )
              (K sat K sat )
              (Theta res 0 [<fraction>])
              (h b h b )
              (l 0.5 [])
              (Theta b Theta b )
              (K b K b )
              (n n )
              (n ma n ma )
              (enable K macro true)
              (enable Theta macro true) >

attrs.doc:
Pressure at boundary point of change between matrix and macropores do-
        mains.

sections.name: M vGp
sections.desc:
van Genuchten retention curve model with Mualem theory. A p m (h) function is
multiplied to the conductivity to simulate the change near maropores.
   p m = (1/(-h X + 1))f ; h > h m p m = (1/(-h m X + 1))f ; h <= h m X = 1
   −1
cm See also [Børgesen et al., 2006]

             (Theta res 0 [<fraction>])
             (l 0.5 [])
             (n n )
             (h m h m )
             (f f ) >

sections.name: linear
sections.desc:
Hysteresis using linear transformation.
   Theta* (h) = a Theta (h) + b
   K* (h) = c K (h) + d
   where Theta and K are defined by either ’wet’ or ’dry’.
   ’a’, ’b’, ’c’, and ’d’ are recalculated whenever the node switches between wetting
and drying.
sections.sig:
< linear (d d )
                   (a a )
                   (b b )
                   (debug false)
                   (wet wet )
                   (dry dry )
                   (is wetting is wetting )
                   (c c ) >

attrs.name: dry
attrs.doc: The hydraulic propeties of drying soil.

attrs.name: consolidate factor
attrs.doc: The ratio between consolidated and loose bulk density.

attrs.name: consolidate factor water
attrs.doc:
An additinal water dependent consolitdate factor. This is multiplied with the
        relative water content [0-1] at tillage, and added to ‘consolidate factor’.

attrs.name: delta pmx fixed
attrs.doc:
Fixed value for ’delta pmx’. By default ’delta pmx’ will be calculated from
        clay content and dry bulk density.

attrs.name: time consolidation
attrs.doc:
Controls consolidation as a function of passing time. consolidation = max * (1
        - exp (- time consolidation * day count)) Larger values, faster consolidation.

attrs.name: average depth
attrs.doc:
Average depth of horizon (positive). Used for estimating ’CECr’ iff unspeci-
        fied. If unspecified, the value from ’Soil’ is used.

attrs.name: CECr
attrs.doc:
Ratio of the cation exchange content of the clay (CECc) to the clay content.
        Used for calculating ’consolidated bulk density’, iff unspecified. By default
        calculated from ’average depth’, CEC, and texture.
        If you have not specified ’CEC’ in the horizon, setting ’CECr’ to 50.0 will
        make most sense due to the way CEC is estimated from texture.

attrs.name: consolidated bulk density
attrs.doc:
Consolidated dry bulk density after rain and time. By default, this will be
        calculated from texture, CEC, and depth.

attrs.name: p t
attrs.doc:
Dry bulk density after last tillage. By default, this will be consolidated dry
        bulk density per wepp.

attrs.name: delta pmx
attrs.doc: Potential dry bulk density change due to rain.

attrs.name: delta pc
attrs.doc: Potential dry bulk density change due to time.

attrs.name: br
attrs.doc: Burried residue 0-15 cm at last tillage.

attrs.name: allow negative delta pc
attrs.doc: Allow ’delta pc’ to be negative after tillage.

attrs.name: crust thickness
attrs.doc: Thickness of soil layer that form crust after rain.

attrs.name: day count
attrs.doc: Number of days since last tillage.

attrs.name: E a
attrs.doc: Energy in rain since last tillage.

attrs.name: freeze effect
attrs.doc:
Maximum decrease of bulk density from frost. The freeze effect works by
    decreasing ‘R c’. ‘R c’ will never be decreased below zero.

attrs.name: freeze on
attrs.doc:
Volumetric ice content above this will activate the frozen state. The freeze
    effect will be activated if the soil is not already frozen.

attrs.name: freeze off
attrs.doc: Volumetric ice content below this will deactivate frozen state.

attrs.name: frozen
attrs.doc:
True if the soil is considered frozen. The soil will be considered frozen after the
    volumetric ice content reaches above ‘freeze on’, and will stay frozen until the
    volumetric ice content fall below ‘freeze off’. When the soil enter the frozen
    state the ‘freeze effect’ trigger.
